metric.name: runtime_majority_share
metric.loc_definition: Physical lines with at least one non-comment token; blank lines and comments excluded. Python docstrings count as code lines. Rust doc and block comments do not.
metric.runtime_scope: Production functions/modules synchronously used from request admission through decision, authorization/consume, process/tool dispatch, response enforcement and owned cleanup, for the product runtime roots: hook HTTP/CLI events, guard-run, direct command/runtime evaluation, package shims/protect/launch, MCP proxy/surface/tool calls and supported direct/frozen routes.
metric.global_exclusions: Tests, fixture constructors, benchmarks, generated catalogs/programs, vendored code, comments/blank lines, offline compiler/authoring-only code, frontend assets, and genuinely asynchronous control/persistence code off the request path.

python.import_policy: static ast closure over eager and lazy imports (TYPE_CHECKING blocks ignored, literal importlib.import_module followed); module granularity

exclusions.reason: Plugin-scanner product (offline scan, scoring, reporting); reached from the package __init__/CLI hub or AIBOM inventory but never invoked on a request-admission-to-enforcement route.

AIBOM inventory/export and trust-metadata reporting; control-plane reads for dashboards/cloud sync, not on the enforcement path. aibom_detection and the inventory_contract fingerprint/model modules stay in scope: adapter detect() and hashing run synchronously during launch.

Wake-driven/background Cloud Review sync, replay and outbox delivery; asynchronous persistence and network delivery outside the synchronous request path. runtime/exact_cloud_review.py, exact_cloud_review_apply.py and exact_cloud_review_diagnostics.py hold the exact-review executor, apply and status logic; they are called only from the excluded command queue, executor, transport, cloud-review settings, connect-time consent and native-workspace-review modules. In-scope code reads constants from them (store_native_workspace_review's revocation state key) and review_exact_capability_advertisement calls _verified_capability and _capability_digest from exact_cloud_review.py to build the queue-eligibility advertisement. That call is reached only through review_contracts.build_local_review_request_claim, whose callers are the background claim paths (cloud_review_event_projection, local_request_snapshots listing for sync, and exact_cloud_review_apply); it is asynchronous claim projection and is not invoked from hook admission, decision, consume or dispatch.

Guard Cloud command-queue worker and executors; remote job processing, not request-path enforcement. runtime/command_capability.py holds the queue capability verification and job authorization; its only in-scope caller is approvals._build_runtime_snapshot, which adds the informational cloud_command_capability field to the approval-center runtime snapshot. That snapshot is built only by the dashboard runtime read route and the `approvals` CLI status read, never from hook admission, decision, consume or dispatch. Through it the module was the sole in-scope importer of review_contracts and review_signature_verification, which leave scope with it.

Extension/contribution authoring, discovery, probing and custom-extension profile management (offline builder or dashboard control plane). Modules the hook evaluation calls synchronously (package_json_scripts, custom_extension_suggestion, mcp_server_contribution, extension_contribution) stay in scope; only continuity sync, catalog sync/handshake and builder/control surfaces are excluded.
Codex/MCP setup, host inventory and registry browsing; configuration management, not enforcement.

Guard self-update orchestration (release download, staging, desktop apply, repair); CLI/daemon lifecycle, not request path. onefile_open_paths.py is reached only from GuardDaemonServer._reclaim_onefile_extraction_dirs_once, the hourly (3600 s) _onefile_extraction_reclaim_loop thread, and the excluded repair engine.

Install/uninstall/doctor/connect/pairing/OAuth/desktop-bootstrap CLI flows and repair/inverse lifecycle. codex_hook_recovery.py/codex_hook_rollback.py are the hook-publication journal, called only from CodexHarnessAdapter._write_authenticated_hook_config_owned, prepare_* migration/backup functions, prepare_install, the shim and cursor prepare functions and the excluded repair/inverse modules. commands_remove_hooks, hook_removal_presence, daemon_stop and commands_repair back the uninstall/repair CLI commands and are imported only by the commands_support facade and the excluded parser/dispatchers.

Argparse construction, Rich rendering and onboarding/status presentation for CLI subcommands that are not runtime routes. cli/render.py stays in scope because hook responses are redacted and emitted through it; only the doctor/uninstall renderers are excluded. commands_support_service.py (service login/status/sync, daemon start/stop/status handlers) is imported only by the commands_support facade and the excluded admin, cloud and records dispatchers.

Managed-device health-lease reporting, lifecycle and removal authorization; cadence-driven machine reporting independent of harness activity. Managed-policy loading (mdm.policy, contracts, network, file locks, device-key and integrity helpers) stays in scope because config loading and the daemon invoke it synchronously during hook handling.
Approval-center/dashboard daemon APIs and daemon lifecycle plumbing (local CLI grants API, command-activity API, diagnostics, reapers); control plane served beside, not inside, the hook route.

Dashboard read routes and their support handlers split out of daemon/server.py: extension-control, runtime, inventory, settings, update, request-queue, receipt, policy, evidence and command-activity GET routes, plus the request list, capabilities, operator health, MCP policy request read, static asset, dashboard shell and event stream handlers. Each is reached only from an explicit /v1 GET branch (or a static dashboard path) dispatched by do_GET after the dashboard token check. Evidence: the transitive self-call closure of _handle_runtime_hook, _handle_runtime_hook_fast, _handle_hook_readiness, _execute_runtime_hook and _handle_daemon_identity_challenge contains none of the moved methods, and hook routes are POST-only so do_GET never reaches the hook path.

Daemon control-plane routes split out of daemon/server.py: package-firewall and supply-chain actions, Guard Cloud connect and dashboard reconnect, headless app actions and receipts, harness/notification/insights/read-state routes, protection-repair and settings routes, and the headless cloud-sync queue and connect-state machines, plus the POST control-route dispatch chain (server_control_routes_post.py: extension-control, local-CLI, settings import, package actions, policy, request-resolution and the remaining /v1 control routes), and the handler bodies behind those routes (server_control_policy.py, server_control_sync.py, server_control_operations.py and server_control_health.py: policy decisions and approval-gate routes, headless policy sync and cloud-exception sync, operation and insight routes, and runtime health, containment and catalog responses). Each is reached only from a /v1 control route dispatched by do_GET/do_POST or from the daemon's background cloud-sync loop; do_POST keeps the origin check, route-class authentication, request-body parsing, daemon identity proof and the /v1/hooks routes in server.py. Evidence: the transitive self-call closure of _handle_runtime_hook, _handle_runtime_hook_fast, _handle_hook_readiness, _execute_runtime_hook and the _runtime_hook_* helpers contains none of the moved methods, and none of the moved module-level functions is referenced from those methods. Helpers shared with the admission path or the server (server_common.py: logger, clock, local-URL builder, string-dict guard, settings response shaper) stay in scope.

Core-owned runtime transition coordination, qualification and capture; one-shot activation lifecycle rather than per-request enforcement. runtime_transition.py (RuntimeTransition, TransitionFile, TransitionError, assert_transition_mutation_allowed) is reached only from install, uninstall, prepare, migrate and repair functions: adapters/base.py (PreparedHarnessInstall.publish, prepare_install, _owned_adapter_mutation), the adapters' prepare_install/install/uninstall/_install_owned/_uninstall_owned/prepare_codex_* methods, cursor_hooks._prepare_cursor_hooks, codex_hook_manifest.prepare_authenticated_hook_*, codex_hook_integrity._ordinary_hook_writer, shims.prepare_guard_shim/install_guard_shim/remove_guard_shim/ensure_guard_shim_path_in_shell_profile, store_cloud_events.set_managed_install (called only by install/bootstrap/paseo install), and the excluded transition coordinator modules. No hook, run, protect or MCP route calls it.

hol-guard-secrets argument parsing and text rendering; separate product entry point, not a Guard runtime route. Detection, repository/staged scans and pre-commit hooks run in the native secrets-cli command. public_rule_catalog.py is the static public rule listing; cli.py reaches the package only through main() for the `secrets` subcommand.

Python string templates that emit TypeScript/JS/shell harness hook assets at install time; generated artifacts, not Python executed on the request path. The current Pi extension emitters (pi_extension_source*.py: header, body, tail, shared-v1 and runtime variants, rendered by managed_extension_source for install, update and drift comparison) and pi_extension_runtime_ownership.py (which only resolves the Guard CLI command and recovery arguments embedded in that generated TypeScript) are the same kind of module as the previous-extension emitters already listed here; their only importers are the Pi adapter, its support shim and the update command (extension install, drift check and update), plus the emitters themselves.

Cloud connect, OAuth refresh/DPoP, receipt, runtime-session, supply-chain-bundle and policy-bundle sync transport (runtime/runner.py). Every public entry point (sync_receipts, sync_runtime_session, sync_supply_chain_bundle, sync_local_guard_cloud_proof, prepare_guard_cloud_connect_authorization, repair_guard_cloud_connect_storage, the cloud-review and command-queue workers and the daemon's cloud policy-bundle and managed-controls delivery handlers that import its urlopen/auth/bundle helpers) runs from `guard connect`/`guard sync`, the cloud-review sync worker or the command-queue loop, never inside hook admission, decision or enforcement. The Rust runtime has no HTTP client, so the network, token refresh and retry loop stay in Python by design; the policy computation inside it (payload shaping, scrubbing, cursor/ack arithmetic, verdict digests, bundle verification) already runs in the resident through runner_native_sync/runner_native_authority. The only request-adjacent caller is the Hermes launch credential lookup (guard_run_launch._resolve_hermes_guard_access_token), which reads the cached token and, when it is absent or near expiry, runs the same OAuth refresh HTTP request as `guard sync` before the harness starts. That refresh is network transport the Rust runtime cannot perform; the lookup is best-effort, runs once at the execution boundary after the authority verdict, and never decides admission. The run-side lookup wrapper stays in scope.

Explicit and periodic Guard repair: `guard repair` (cli/commands_repair), POST /v1/repair and the removal endpoint (daemon/repair_api via _handle_repair_api) and the 600 s repair self-check thread (daemon/repair_self_check started by _start_repair_self_check). None runs inside hook admission, decision or enforcement. resident_state_prune.py and daemon/runtime_repair.py are reached only from repair_engine (repair_native_runtime, repair_daemon) and the daemon package's lazy export used by the repair CLI handler.

Thin wrappers that invoke the third-party Cisco skill and MCP analyzers in a bounded scanner subprocess and normalize their raw output into Finding records. They decide nothing: which roots may be scanned, every containment verdict, the finding-to-signal mapping and the policy action are owned by the resident cisco_preflight operation (guard-runtime cisco_plan, cisco_containment and cisco_evidence), which never spawns analyzers. Reached from guard/native_cisco_preflight.py (the analyzer step between the resident plan and evidence queries) and from the plugin-scanner product. The exclusion is whole-path rather than function-level because the in-scope transport imports the analyzer runners, which a function exclusion forbids.

Best-effort janitor that retires guard daemons and clears daemon state leaked by ephemeral (pytest temp) guard homes. It is scheduled once per interval on a daemon thread from ensure_guard_daemon (manager._schedule_stale_ephemeral_guard_daemon_reap), never joins, never gates the caller, and acts only on other homes (the caller's own home is excluded). It runs no hook admission, decision, authorization or enforcement, and the manager reaches it through a late-bound facade.

Static protection-capability payloads for the dashboard and settings views. Its only callers are daemon/server_common.py's _settings_response_payload (called only from server_dashboard_runtime_read.py, server_control_repair.py and server_control_sync.py), server_dashboard_runtime_read.py and the excluded approvals runtime snapshot; no hook or tool request reads it.

reviewed_runtime.reason: Reviewed adapter family package initializers introduced by the source-layout refactor. Each contains only its package docstring; these modules are reached through lazy hook imports and remain counted in runtime scope. No runtime behavior is excluded.

Retained conservatively in runtime scope: managed_controls_policy_bundle lazily reaches cloud policy synchronization and its catalog page/provider transport. Count these complete Python adapters, including transport and native dispatch, rather than excluding shared modules reached through policy authority. Native catalog validation remains counted in Rust.

Retained conservatively in runtime scope: generated_command_catalog and native_command_control_binding reach authenticated pack metadata, activation projection and recovery through lazy imports. Count the complete shared delivery modules, including preparation and transport helpers, rather than exclude code reachable through those authority boundaries. Pack admission and hook evaluation remain native.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: cli/commands_support_runtime_artifacts reaches these at module load when it builds runtime artifacts; the resident now recognises non-executing GitHub Actions reads. github_command_capabilities returns unknown when the native GitHub classifier is unavailable and never re-derives a capability in Python. The sensitive-request classifiers that used to reach them eagerly now run in the resident, so they are reached through that lazily loaded artifact module and stay counted.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: the routine local runner verdict that used to import node_semver_spec_matches now runs in the resident package intent parser, so the artifact module no longer reaches this. scripts/record_direct_tool_vectors binds node_semver_spec_matches into the services it replays direct tool vectors through, which is a recording harness rather than an enforcement path; the module stays counted until that harness reads the native verdict.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: Copilot hook processing captures local retry correlation metadata through capture_retry_lineage. The identifiers are diagnostic inputs, not authorization. Native continuation finalization preserves the first valid lineage when updating an operation; the remaining Python capture path stays counted.
Reviewed: module is a decision, parser/scanner, transport, process-dispatch or containment component invoked by a runtime route.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: the direct-evidence drain hands each MCP tool call the native relay decided to the receipt writers the Python MCP proxy calls. It validates the queued record, records a forward or block exactly as the resident decided it, and drops any record it cannot validate; it never recomputes a verdict.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: the package half of the same drain. It writes the receipt the proxy's package lane writes, against the package request's own artifact, rebuilding that artifact from the parser input the resident read and dropping any record whose rebuilt artifact is not the one the resident decided; it never recomputes a verdict.

Reviewed: cli support/router/render: hook payload, interaction, runtime resolution and policy, permission store, connect and workspace helpers, the command router and lifecycle gate (run/protect), and cli/render.py. Reached synchronously from cli/commands_support_hook_payload and commands_hook_native_pipeline on every native hook request, and from commands_router.run_guard_command for run/protect. render.py is kept whole because its native-hook emitters share the module with presentation code; function-level scoping is a follow-up.

Reviewed: adapters: harness registry targets (codex, grok, zcode, mcp_servers and the MCP proxy launcher selection, cursor native approval, hermes file inspection, capability_report, attestation and path helpers). Loaded through the dynamic adapter registry and reached from approvals.py, cursor_hooks, hook workers and launch_command for run/protect. Install/diagnostics methods share the classes with the launch and approval paths, so the files stay whole in scope.

Reviewed: codex hook inventory, identity, sources, trust, registration, owner commands/preflight and health modules: codex_hook_trust_stale is called from codex_native_hook_state, which gates launch_command/preview_launch_commands for codex, and it imports registration and owner_commands; runtime_trust is used by frozen_codex_runtime.trusted_hook_launch; inventory/identity/sources are used by the same adapter. codex_hook_owner_preflight and codex_hook_health are tiny status/install-only modules left in scope under the in-doubt rule. codex_hook_self_binding and codex_hook_owned_paths decide whether an existing Codex handler belongs to this installation, which registration consults before it will replace or refuse one, and codex_hook_owner_message writes the refusal that decision produces; all three are reached from the same adapter and stay in scope with it.

Reviewed: daemon client and peer modules: client/response_bounds are the hook-to-daemon transport; runtime_peer/live_identity authenticate the live daemon; recovery_lifecycle is invoked from daemon/manager on hook-failure recovery; policy_authority_client is called from local_supply_chain; claude_permission_request is called from hook_worker.

Reviewed: runtime support modules used by supply-chain evaluation, contained execution, local-CLI/MCP grant decisions and secret-file-request services: js_semver, npm_policy_range, lockfile/manifest evaluation, package_json_scripts, source_paths/skill_paths, workspace_snapshot_inputs, contained_test_hook/wrapper/run_directory/command_prefix/authority, oci isolation, extension and mcp_server contribution, embedded_script_evidence, executable_flag_contract, mcp_connection_identity, and skill_protection (skill-content findings for the MCP skill firewall). Each is imported by an in-scope decision, parser or containment module on the hook/run path.

Reviewed: shared policy, inventory, store and consumer modules: consumer/service (runtime runner), capabilities, product_model (argv harness dispatch in the top-level CLI on every invocation), local_cli_* trust decisions (native_mcp_tool_policy), business_policy_document_import (policy snapshot publisher and recovery), store_* mixins on the policy/MCP/extension paths, skill_document_evidence, trust_metadata_boundary, inventory_item_description, text.py, runtime_transition_hook_probe (daemon/server), cloud_exceptions (store_cloud_events) and policy_bundle_decisions (local_supply_chain policy-bundle handling).

Reviewed: windows_current_user_sid and its token-API loader: native_policy_snapshot_windows_support lazily imports it to bind the Windows policy snapshot owner, so it runs when a snapshot is written; the rest of device_key_native is excluded by mdm-device-key-native-signing.

Reviewed: the guard mcp serve stdio server (GuardMCPServer, tool registry, adapters, sanitizers, schemas) and its policy-authoring tools. The scope definition lists the MCP surface and tool calls as runtime, and these tools are invoked by coding agents with Guard-authored results, so they stay in scope even though the serve command is launched interactively rather than from a hook.

Reviewed: adapter implementations behind the harness registry. Adapters normalize harness payloads into hook requests, so they sit on the hook path, and hook-path authority is never excluded. Install and setup methods that have a function_exclusions entry are excluded as install_config, not hook path; install helpers without an entry (for example in the Cline, OpenCode and OpenClaw support modules) stay counted, which understates the Rust share.

Reviewed: claude_code adapter and its inventory/skill-directory and aibom detection helpers. The Claude hook client no longer imports them; they load lazily from the frozen hook and the adapter registry for install, inventory and approval flows, not per tool call.

Reviewed: policy bundle v2 evidence and clock helpers. policy_bundle_trusted_keys loads the module through a literal importlib.import_module call when it builds the native verification request for a signed policy bundle, so it is runtime policy-bundle verification and stays counted.

Reviewed: GitHub workflow capability preflight and approval records. commands_hook_native_eval.py imports github_workflow_runtime to resolve the workflow capability preflight on a native hook call, and commands_support_runtime_policy.py reads GitHubWorkflowApprovalRecord when it resolves runtime policy, so both are hook-path runtime and stay counted. approvals.py used to pull them in eagerly; they are now reached only through these lazy hook-path imports.

Reviewed: fail-closed bridge to the native GitHub CLI classifier. github_shell_capabilities.py classifies gh commands through it while a hook evaluates a shell request, so it is hook-path runtime and stays counted. When the resident cannot answer it returns the review floor instead of re-deriving the capability in Python.

Reviewed: synced policy payload. commands_support_runtime_resolution.py builds the synced policy payload from it while resolving a runtime decision, so it is runtime policy resolution and stays counted. approvals.py used to pull it in eagerly; it is now reached only through that lazy runtime path.

Reviewed: managed install proof binding and verification. PaseoHarnessAdapter.detect (adapters/paseo.py) calls paseo_install.provider_status, which runs verify_managed_install_proof to report each provider's protection status. Adapter detection stays in scope for every harness (the adapter setup exclusions leave detect counted), so the verifier stays counted with it. Binding (bind_managed_install_proof) is reached only from the excluded install paths.

Reviewed: Codex hook event names, manifest, integrity, compatibility and install transaction modules. The Codex hook bridge no longer imports them at load; launch validation and the installer load them lazily. The event-name tuple was previously imported eagerly by the Python binding-capture modules, which now run natively, and the manifest still loads it when launch trust reads the hook manifest. They stay counted as runtime because launch trust still runs them until the native resident owns that lane.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: cli/render.py imports it at module load so the status and doctor panels report whether the configured protection posture is actually in effect. It reads the harness rows the adapters already produced and decides what the panel says; no admission, authority or enforcement decision reads it.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: consumer/service reaches the low-trust review floor lazily when it decides a first-seen or changed skill, MCP server or plugin. The floor reads a public HOL Registry trust score with a bounded, cached lookup and can only raise an action; native composition still decides the result.

Reviewed and retained in runtime scope: the bound-Bash review path reaches these lazily from hook_native_review_approval and cli/commands_dispatch_local. They carry the IPC transport and the projection of a native decision to the caller; the authorization itself, the content binding and the launch barrier stay in guard-runtime, and the sink refuses to act on a saved decision it cannot read, match or verify. Count these complete Python modules rather than exclude code reached through the native owner's reply boundary.

tests.note: repository-level Python tests, not part of the package

function_exclusions.reason: Whole-machine ownership and ACL verification for the managed-device integrity snapshot. It runs when the health lease reports, when removal is authorized and for the guard mdm command, on their own cadence rather than during hook handling.
function_exclusions.evidence: verify_protected_ownership_and_acl and OwnershipAclVerification are called only from mdm/integrity.py (whose machine_integrity_snapshot is imported only by mdm/user_health.py, mdm/health_lease.py and cli/commands_dispatch_mdm.py) and mdm/removal.py (mdm-health). The per-path helpers that in-scope mdm/managed_file_trust.py imports (_PathSurface, _run_windows_acl_payload, _verify_macos_surface, _windows_filesystem_chain, _windows_result) stay in scope. The report validates this reference closure on every run.

function_exclusions.reason: Trust-backend selection and the spawned backend check worker behind the guard trust command.
function_exclusions.evidence: TrustBackend, select_trust_backend, run_trust_backend_check, degraded_reason_for_backend_error and the backend errors are used only by local_trust_controller.py, which only cli/commands_dispatch_trust.py imports. TrustStatus and the POLICY_INTEGRITY_* constants that the store modules import stay in scope. The report validates this reference closure on every run.

function_exclusions.reason: Preparing an authenticated Codex hook manifest repair. It runs only from the Codex authority repair flow.
function_exclusions.evidence: PreparedCodexHookRepair and prepare_authenticated_hook_manifest_repair are used only by codex_hook_repair_request.py, codex_hook_repair.py and cli/codex_authority_repair.py (install-uninstall-doctor). The manifest build, publication, baseline and live verification functions that adapters/codex.py imports stay in scope. The report validates this reference closure on every run.

function_exclusions.reason: Request-body, request-list, harness-action, headless-action, detection-status and supply-chain helpers for daemon control-plane and dashboard routes.
function_exclusions.evidence: Each excluded public helper is called only from daemon/server_control_policy.py, server_control_misc.py, server_control_headless.py, server_control_supply_chain.py (daemon-control-plane-routes) or daemon/server_dashboard_support.py (daemon-dashboard-read-routes). HandlerDecision, NativeDaemonHandlerError and native_events_cursor, which daemon/server.py imports, stay in scope. The report validates this reference closure on every run.

function_exclusions.reason: Evidence counting, serialization and JSON/CSV export (with formula-injection sanitizing) for the dashboard records view.
function_exclusions.evidence: count_evidence, evidence_record_to_dict, export_evidence_json and export_evidence_csv are called only from daemon/server_dashboard_records_read.py (daemon-dashboard-read-routes). Evidence schema setup, storage, listing and clearing, which the store and runtime modules import, stay in scope. The report validates this reference closure on every run.

function_exclusions.reason: Rich and plain-text renderers, panel and table builders, and the renderer dispatch tables that format Guard command results for a human terminal. They compute no verdicts and read no stores; they only lay out an already-built payload.
function_exclusions.evidence: The retained reference closure of every symbol other modules import from render.py (_redact_payload, _render_redacted_json_payload, emit_guard_payload) contains none of the excluded symbols except through emit_guard_payload, whose as_json=True branch (the only branch the hook protocol uses: commands_support_hook_payload.py writes JSON through _redact_payload and _render_redacted_json_payload directly) never reads them. The excluded symbols are reached only from emit_guard_payload's as_json=False branch through the _RENDERERS and _PLAIN_TEXT_RENDERERS tables. The report validates this reference closure on every run.

function_exclusions.evidence: The default prepare_install, install and uninstall are invoked only from the excluded install, uninstall and repair command dispatchers. No retained runtime code reads these attributes. The report validates that no retained symbol or in-scope module references the excluded names.
